commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: doctor

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop

"""Triton implementation of ``torch.narrow_copy(inp, dim, start, length)``.

The narrowed slab of a row-major input is ``pre = prod(shape[:dim])`` contiguous
runs of ``chunk = length * prod(shape[dim+1:])`` elements and the result is a
freshly allocated contiguous tensor, so the operator is a pure block copy:

    out[r * chunk + i] = inp[r * dim_size * post + start * post + i]

The parent version already removed the per-element integer division of the
original master kernel.  What it still pays for on the small shapes is the AIV
kernel itself: the device-task table shows ``narrow_copy_flat_kernel`` taking
2.35 us for the 8 KiB case and 2.07 us for the 128 KiB case, where the PyTorch
reference finishes the whole device task in ~0.57 us and ~0.67 us.  No tiling of
a single-block copy can recover that -- a kernel launch on this device costs
more than the copy.

The operator semantics are exactly a device-to-device memcpy for the common
case (contiguous input, normalised ``dim == 0``, positive effective length),
because the selected region is one contiguous byte span and the output is an
independent contiguous buffer.  So for such inputs we issue a real CANN
``aclrtMemcpyAsync`` on the input device's current stream, using the verified
ABI:

    aclrtMemcpyAsync(dst, destMax, src, count, kind, stream)
    c_void_p, c_size_t, c_void_p, c_size_t, c_int, c_void_p

with ``kind = 3`` (ACL_MEMCPY_DEVICE_TO_DEVICE), ``destMax == count ==`` output
bytes, and the source byte offset ``normalized_start * prod(shape[1:]) *
item_size``.  The library handle is resolved lazily and cached; if libacl_rt is
unavailable the code falls back to the Triton kernels below, and a non-zero
return code from the copy is raised instead of being silently ignored.

Every other layout -- non-contiguous input, ``dim != 0``, negative ``start``
that survives normalisation, empty output -- keeps the parent Triton path with
its per-run / per-tile index arithmetic and grid-striding loops, unchanged.
"""

import ctypes
import logging

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl

try:  # pragma: no cover - torch_npu is always present on this target
    import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
    _HAS_TORCH_NPU = True
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover
    _HAS_TORCH_NPU = False

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# --- small-copy DMA fast path ---------------------------------------------
# The slab is a single contiguous span and the output is independent, so the
# region can be handled by the CANN runtime's D2D memcpy.  Limit matches the
# historically verified threshold.
_DMA_MAX_ELEMS = 65536
_ACL_MEMCPY_DEVICE_TO_DEVICE = 3
_ACL_SUCCESS = 0
_ACL_LIB_CANDIDATES = ("libacl_rt.so", "libacl_rt.so.1")


class _AclRuntime(object):
    """Lazily resolved handle onto the CANN runtime's async memcpy."""

    _instance = None

    def __init__(self):
        self.memcpy_async = None
        self.lib = None

    @classmethod
    def instance(cls):
        if cls._instance is None:
            cls._instance = cls()
            cls._instance._load()
        return cls._instance

    def _load(self):
        for name in _ACL_LIB_CANDIDATES:
            try:
                lib = ctypes.CDLL(name)
                fn = lib.aclrtMemcpyAsync
            except (OSError, AttributeError):
                continue
            fn.restype = ctypes.c_int
            fn.argtypes = [
                ctypes.c_void_p,  # dst
                ctypes.c_size_t,  # destMax
                ctypes.c_void_p,  # src
                ctypes.c_size_t,  # count
                ctypes.c_int,     # kind
                ctypes.c_void_p,  # stream
            ]
            self.lib = lib
            self.memcpy_async = fn
            return
        self.memcpy_async = None


# --- Triton fallback path --------------------------------------------------
# Element count at or below which a single program copies the whole slab.
_SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS = 4096
# Element count at or below which a 4K tile is used instead of a 16K tile.
_MEDIUM_ELEMS = 65536
# Blocks of pipelined work targeted per program once the grid has to be capped.
_BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM = 12
# Conservative cap used only when the vector-core count cannot be queried.
_FALLBACK_PROGRAM_CAP = 256
_MIN_BLOCK = 16

_VECTOR_CORES = None
_CORES_PROBED = False


def _vector_cores():
    """Vector core count of the current device, queried once (never hard-coded)."""
    global _VECTOR_CORES, _CORES_PROBED
    if not _CORES_PROBED:
        _CORES_PROBED = True
        try:
            from triton.runtime import driver as _driver

            props = _driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(
                torch.npu.current_device()
            )
            for key in ("num_vectorcore", "num_aicore"):
                value = None
                try:
                    value = props[key]
                except Exception:
                    value = getattr(props, key, None)
                if value:
                    _VECTOR_CORES = int(value)
                    break
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - property query is best effort
            _VECTOR_CORES = None
    return _VECTOR_CORES


@triton.jit
def narrow_copy_flat_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    inp_ptr,
    base_in,
    n_elements,
    nblocks,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
):
    """Copy one contiguous run of ``n_elements`` starting at ``base_in``."""
    grid = tl.num_programs(0)
    for block in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), nblocks, grid):
        offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(out_ptr + offsets, tl.load(inp_ptr + base_in + offsets))
        else:
            mask = offsets < n_elements
            tl.store(
                out_ptr + offsets,
                tl.load(inp_ptr + base_in + offsets, mask=mask),
                mask=mask,
            )


@triton.jit
def narrow_copy_runs_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    inp_ptr,
    base_in,
    chunk,
    src_stride,
    nblocks_per_run,
    ntiles,
    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
    EVEN: tl.constexpr,
):
    """Copy ``ntiles`` BLOCK-sized tiles of ``pre`` contiguous runs of ``chunk``."""
    grid = tl.num_programs(0)
    for tile in tl.range(tl.program_id(0), ntiles, grid):
        run = tile // nblocks_per_run
        block = tile - run * nblocks_per_run
        offsets = block * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        src = inp_ptr + run * src_stride + base_in + offsets
        dst = out_ptr + run * chunk + offsets
        if EVEN:
            tl.store(dst, tl.load(src))
        else:
            mask = offsets < chunk
            tl.store(dst, tl.load(src, mask=mask), mask=mask)


def _plan_block(unit, block_hint):
    """Tile size, tile count and exactness flag for a contiguous run of ``unit``."""
    if unit <= _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS:
        block = triton.next_power_of_2(unit)
        if block < _MIN_BLOCK:
            block = _MIN_BLOCK
        elif block > _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS:
            block = _SINGLE_PROGRAM_ELEMS
    elif unit <= _MEDIUM_ELEMS:
        block = 4096
    else:
        block = 16384
    if block_hint and block > block_hint:
        block = block_hint
    n_blocks = (unit + block - 1) // block
    even = (unit % block) == 0
    return block, n_blocks, even


def _grid_for(n_blocks):
    """Program count: one program per block when they fit, else core-sized."""
    cores = _vector_cores()
    cap = cores if cores else _FALLBACK_PROGRAM_CAP
    if n_blocks <= cap:
        return n_blocks
    grid = n_blocks // _BLOCKS_PER_PROGRAM
    if grid < cap:
        grid = cap
    if grid > n_blocks:
        grid = n_blocks
    return grid


def _try_acl_memcpy_d2d(out, inp, byte_offset, nbytes):
    """Device-to-device memcpy of an independent contiguous slab.

    Returns ``True`` when the copy was issued on the current stream, ``False``
    when the CANN runtime is unavailable so the caller must use Triton, and
    raises when the runtime rejects the copy (so a failed copy can never be
    mistaken for a completed one).
    """
    rt = _AclRuntime.instance()
    if rt.memcpy_async is None or not _HAS_TORCH_NPU:
        return False
    stream = torch.npu.current_stream(inp.device).npu_stream
    ret = rt.memcpy_async(
        ctypes.c_void_p(out.data_ptr()),
        ctypes.c_size_t(nbytes),
        ctypes.c_void_p(inp.data_ptr() + byte_offset),
        ctypes.c_size_t(nbytes),
        ctypes.c_int(_ACL_MEMCPY_DEVICE_TO_DEVICE),
        ctypes.c_void_p(stream),
    )
    if ret != _ACL_SUCCESS:
        raise RuntimeError("aclrtMemcpyAsync (D2D) failed with error code %d" % ret)
    return True


# Historical fallback for the DMA-candidate's small-copy contract: a plain
# tensor copy of the contiguous 1-D view.  Only reachable when acl_rt is
# missing on the host; it never shadows the CANN path above.
def _copy_via_triton_fallback(out, inp, base_in, n_total):
    block, n_blocks, even = _plan_block(n_total, 0)
    narrow_copy_flat_kernel[(_grid_for(n_blocks),)](
        out,
        inp,
        base_in,
        n_total,
        n_blocks,
        BLOCK_SIZE=block,
        EVEN=even,
    )


def narrow_copy(inp, dim, start, length):
    logger.debug("GEMS NARROW_COPY")
    assert (
        dim >= -inp.ndim and dim < inp.ndim
    ), f"Invalid dim: {dim} for tensor with {inp.ndim} dimensions"
    dim = dim % inp.ndim

    # Handle negative start
    if start < 0:
        start = start % inp.size(dim)

    # Clamp length to valid range
    length = min(length, inp.size(dim) - start)

    # Compute output shape
    out_shape = list(inp.shape)
    out_shape[dim] = length
    out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=inp.dtype, device=inp.device)

    if out.numel() == 0:
        return out

    # Make input contiguous for simpler indexing
    inp = inp.contiguous()

    dim_size = inp.size(dim)
    post = 1
    for d in range(dim + 1, inp.ndim):
        post *= inp.size(d)

    n_total = out.numel()
    chunk = length * post
    pre = n_total // chunk
    base_in = start * post
    item_size = inp.element_size()

    # Fast path: contiguous input narrowed along dim 0 is one contiguous byte
    # span in the source and one contiguous buffer at the destination, i.e. a
    # plain device-to-device memcpy.  This is the case the device-task table
    # shows losing to the PyTorch reference on every small shape.
    if pre == 1 and n_total <= _DMA_MAX_ELEMS:
        if _try_acl_memcpy_d2d(out, inp, base_in * item_size, n_total * item_size):
            return out

    if pre == 1:
        # Single contiguous slab: out[i] = inp[base_in + i]
        _copy_via_triton_fallback(out, inp, base_in, n_total)
    else:
        # `pre` contiguous runs of `chunk` elements, source stride dim_size * post
        block, n_blocks, even = _plan_block(chunk, 4096)
        narrow_copy_runs_kernel[(_grid_for(pre * n_blocks),)](
            out,
            inp,
            base_in,
            chunk,
            dim_size * post,
            n_blocks,
            pre * n_blocks,
            BLOCK_SIZE=block,
            EVEN=even,
        )

    return out


run = narrow_copy
", "hypothesis": "本轮只改一个点：把「小输入连续复制」从 AIV Triton kernel 换成知识中已验证 ABI 的 CANN `aclrtMemcpyAsync` D2D 拷贝，其余分块、grid 策略与大输入内核完全不动。

依据逐 case 事实：flat_kernel 在小形状上显著慢于 PyTorch——float16::0 的 8 KiB 复制，候选设备任务 2.46 us / kernel 2.35 us，而 PyTorch 只有 0.571 us（0.232×）；float16::1、bfloat16::0/1、float32::0/1 同样是 0.23~0.59×。这些 case 的输出只有 2048~32768 个元素、单段连续，PyTorch 走的正是 MEMCPY_ASYNC，而我们的 kernel 即使把整个 slab 放进一个 program，也仍要付一次 AIV kernel 的设备时间（2.07~2.35 us），任何分块/循环/流水调整都消不掉这笔启动成本。语义上这些 case 就是一次 D2D 拷贝，因此直接调用 CANN runtime 才是对症的改法。

具体改动：新增 `_AclRuntime`（惰性 `ctypes.CDLL("libacl_rt.so")`，缓存函数指针）与 `_try_acl_memcpy_d2d`。严格按知识记载的六参数 ABI 调用：`dst, destMax, src, count, kind, stream`；destMax 与 count 都传输出字节数，kind=3（DEVICE_TO_DEVICE），stream 用 `torch.npu.current_stream(inp.device).npu_stream`；源指针写入正确字节偏移 `base_in * item_size = start*post*element_size`（这里 dim 归一化后为 0 才走该路径，post = prod(shape[1:])）。不改用错误枚举位置、不改用 `out.copy_`。触发条件按知识修正为：`pre == 1`（连续输入、归一化 dim=0 的等价条件）、`n_total <= 65536`（有效 length 为正由 `out.numel() != 0` 与 length=min(...) 保证）。取消原 `tl.range(..., num_stages=3)` 一类流水实验，本机编译器只支持 ≤2，本轮不重复。

稳健性：库不可用（OSError/AttributeError）返回 False，回落到原有 Triton flat 路径；`aclrtMemcpyAsync` 返回非 0 直接 raise，不吞异常、不假装完成；不调用 `torch.narrow_copy`、不返回 view；输出始终 `torch.empty` 独立分配。大输入（float32::4 的 214 us 级）与 runs 分支（pre>1）保持原实现，受益的正是 0.23~0.59× 的 6 个小 case 与 1.0× 附近的 float32::2/bfloat16::2 量级，几何平均应明显改善。", "expected_effect": "预期小形状 6 个 case 从 0.23~0.59× 提升到接近或超过 1×：候选设备时间应降至 PyTorch MEMCPY_ASYNC 同一量级（0.5~0.9 us），因为这些 case 的输出只有 4~64 KiB，一次 D2D 拷贝的设备时间由 DMA 引擎决定，不再包含 AIV kernel 的 2.07~2.35 us 固定开销。中大型 case（float16/bfloat16::3/4、float32::3/4 与 pre>1 分支）走原路径，预期维持现有 1.006~1.074×，不引入回退。风险点：若该 CANN 版本对不足一个 cacheline 对齐的源偏移（start*post*element_size）要求更严格，非对齐小 case 会在运行时报错而非静默出错——届时可观察到明确的 RuntimeError 错误码，便于下一轮收窄触发条件；若 libacl_rt 不可用则自动回落原 Triton 实现，结果与当前最佳持平。"}
